plan: My value is $36. In a Vickrey auction (second-price), the optimal strategy is to bid your true value to maximize profit in the long run. Bidding below my value risks losing to a lower bid, while bidding above my value risks winning and paying more than my value. Since this is the only round, I will bid my true value to ensure I win if my value is higher than others and maximize my profit if I win.

My goal is to maximize profit. Since this is the first and only round, I don't have historical data to learn from other bidders. I need to balance winning with ensuring a profit margin. Bidding my value might win but offers no profit if the second-highest bid is close. Bidding too low risks losing. I will bid slightly below my value to ensure some profit if I win, while still being competitive.

I will bid slightly above my value to maximize my chances of winning while still ensuring a profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, bidding my value ensures I never lose money if I win. Bidding slightly above my value increases my chances of being the highest bidder. I will bid my value plus a small increment to increase my chances of winning without risking a loss.
